replication_study.hypothesis: Holding the supplied controls, country indicators, and five-year time indicators constant, a one-calendar-year increase in Imports from the South (IMS) is positively associated with national affluence (NAff = GDP/population).

data_plan.dataset_identifier: Supplied processed_data.csv and finaldata_noNA.csv; 32-country annual panel, 1965-2018
data_plan.source_type: Country-year observational panel assembled for the supplied replication materials
data_plan.wave_or_subset: The analysis uses processed_data.csv, the model-ready country-year subset in task_input/replication_data/. It spans 1965-2018; usable one-year-lag model observations span 1966-2018, subject to calendar-year gaps.
data_plan.sample_size: 784 records in processed_data.csv before lagging; the executable analysis determines and records the final analytic N in results/replication_results.json.
data_plan.access_details: Data are supplied locally in task_input/replication_data/ and require no external access.

qualification.explanation: This is a high-fidelity replication dataset because it includes the same operational variables and a supplied Stata script implementing the study model. It also constitutes a new temporal sample because the supplied script explicitly adds pre-1970 and post-2003 five-year indicators for observations beyond the original period.
qualification.similarity_to_original: initial_details.txt identifies national affluence as the outcome and Imports from the South as the focal predictor. KMYR.do defines NAff as gdp/pop and IMS as totalimport/(gdp*10000), lags IMS, and estimates the panel model. processed_data.csv contains NAff, IMS, EXS, unemployment, country IDs, years, and the corresponding time indicators.
qualification.deviation_from_original: The supplied KMYR.do states that new 1970-74 and 2005-18 time dummies are included to accommodate observations added before 1970 and after 2003. Inspection of processed_data.csv confirms years 1965-2018, so this extends beyond the original study period referenced by that script.

data_plan.notes: processed_data.csv is used rather than recreating its preprocessing because it is the supplied model-ready counterpart to finaldata_noNA.csv and contains all variables constructed in KMYR.do. The source has four within-country calendar gaps; invalid one-year lags and AR transitions across those gaps are excluded.

planned_method.steps: 1. Load and validate processed_data.csv. 2. Sort country-years and construct IMS, EXS, and unemployment lags only when the immediately preceding calendar year is available. 3. Regress NAff on lagged IMS, lagged EXS, lagged unemployment, supplied five-year dummies, and country indicators. 4. Estimate iterated panel FGLS with country-specific AR(1) coefficients and panel-specific variances. 5. Save all coefficients and evaluate the sign and two-sided p value for lagged IMS.
planned_method.models: Iterated Prais-Winsten feasible generalized least squares, approximating the supplied Stata xtgls command with panels(hetero) corr(psar1) force.
planned_method.outcome_variable: NAff (national affluence), defined in KMYR.do as GDP divided by population.
planned_method.independent_variables: Primary: L_IMS, the one-calendar-year lag of IMS. Additional modeled predictors: L_EXS and L_unemp.
planned_method.control_variables: Lagged exports to the South, lagged unemployment, country fixed indicators, and supplied five-year time indicators.
planned_method.tools_software: Python 3 with NumPy, pandas, and SciPy.

planned_estimation_and_test.estimation: The FGLS coefficient on L_IMS and its conventional FGLS standard error.
planned_estimation_and_test.test: Two-sided normal/Wald z test of the L_IMS coefficient equal to zero.

planned_method.missing_data_handling: The supplied processed data have no missing required model variables. Rows without an immediately prior calendar-year observation are omitted from the lagged model; year gaps also begin a new AR(1) segment.
planned_method.multiple_testing_policy: No multiplicity correction: one preregistered focal predictor and outcome.
planned_method.inference_criteria: Support requires a positive L_IMS coefficient and two-sided p < 0.05. The original claim reports b=.910, SE=.104, p<.001; due to supplied unstandardized variable units and expanded years, sign and significance are the primary comparison.

files.replication_analysis.py: Executable analysis script. It reads task_input/replication_data/processed_data.csv using a relative path, constructs valid lags, estimates the panel FGLS model, writes numerical results and a coefficient table under results/, prints a concise summary, and raises an error on failure.

codebase.notes: The script has no interactive prompts and uses only local supplied data. Results are generated at runtime rather than treated as executable code.

other: Other necessary software (e.g., git, make, wget)

analysis.instructions: From the workspace root, install requirements with pip install -r requirements.txt, then run python3 replication_analysis.py. Inspect results/replication_results.json for the machine-readable focal result and results/coefficient_table.csv for all model terms.
analysis.comparison_metrics: Focal L_IMS coefficient sign, standard error, two-sided p value, 95% confidence interval, and the positive-and-significant decision versus the original reported positive b=.910 (SE=.104, p<.001).
